extracted.intended_audience: LinkedIn members, researchers, journalists, policymakers, and the public interested in platform safety and transparency
extracted.subtask_description: A corporate transparency report describing how LinkedIn detects, enforces, and reports removals of fake accounts, spam/scams, content policy violations, and copyright claims over six-month reporting periods, including counts and system-performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fake profiles policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policies prohibit fake profiles and require that members are real people who represent themselves accurately and contribute authentically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LinkedIn frames fake profiles as disallowed behavior and a breach of community standards; members are expected to represent themselves accurately and behave authentically on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fake accounts detection and removal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Our automated defenses blocked 97.1% of the fake accounts we stopped during the January - June 2025 period, with the remaining 2.9% stopped by our manual investigations and restrictions. 99.5% of the fake accounts were stopped proactively, before a member report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics are reported for the six-month period (Jan–Jun 2025). Emphasizes automated-first strategy, proactive stopping prior to member reports, and ongoing enhancements to defenses. Historical period breakdowns are provided for trend analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spam and scams policy / definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Spam and scams are not permitted on LinkedIn. By far the most common type of inappropriate content we take action on is spam or scam content, which includes inappropriate commercial activity and repetitive communications or invitations, often meant for financial gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines spam/scam by examples (inappropriate commercial activity, repetitive communications/invitations aimed at financial gain). This serves as the standard for identifying disallowed spam/scam content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spam and scams detection and removal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the spam or scam content removed in this reporting period, our automated defenses stopped 98.7% and our teams manually removed the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides automated-vs-manual removal breakdown for spam/scams and supplies period-by-period counts. Includes an explicit correction note for previously reported historical values (e.g., Jan–Jun 2021 spam removals corrected from 232K to 224K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content compliance with Professional Community Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Content on LinkedIn must comply with our Professional Community Policies and we take action if it doesn't. Members can always ask us to take a second look if they believe we made a mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy compliance is the standard for content; enforcement is subject to review and an appeals/second-look process. The report notes increased volume of violative content tied to community growth and improved detection capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content removal counts by reporting period
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of content removed for policy violations are reported by six-month periods (e.g., 2025: Jan–Jun, 2024: Jul–Dec, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report publishes historical removal counts (with period labels) to show trends. It also includes correction notes (e.g., edits to previously reported harassment/abusive content counts for Jan–Jun 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright policy / respect for intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: We respect the intellectual property rights of others and do not allow copyright infringement. Our User Agreement requires members to respect others’ rights and follow the law, including gathering any necessary legal permissions before sharing protected content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the normative requirement for member behavior regarding IP; members must obtain necessary permissions and follow the law before sharing protected works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright takedown reporting metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For each reporting period the report shows: Requests [1], Total infringements reported [2], Reported infringements removed [3], Reported infringements rejected [4], Percentage accepted. Example: 2025 Jan–Jun — Requests: 2,338; Total infringements reported: 2,728; Reported infringements removed: 2,568; Reported infringements rejected: 160; Percentage accepted: 94%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: [1] Requests from copyright owners claiming infringement; [2] Requests often cite multiple infringements; [3] Infringements removed means action was taken; [4] Reported infringements not removed. Historical period-by-period tables are published to show trends and acceptance rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of automated defenses and proactive stopping
rubrics_metrics.description: LinkedIn emphasizes automated defenses that proactively stop the majority of abusive accounts and content (e.g., 97.1% of fake accounts blocked automatically; 98.7% of spam/scam stopped by automated systems in the reporting period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report presents automated detection as the primary enforcement mechanism, supplemented by manual investigations and removals. It highlights proactive stopping prior to member reports as a metric of effectiveness and notes ongoing improvements to technology and messaging defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals / second-look process
rubrics_metrics.description: Members can always ask us to take a second look if they believe we made a mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a procedural remedy for members affected by enforcement (an appeals or review pathway), though detailed appeal procedures are referenced via links (e.g., Help Center) rather than fully enumerated in the report text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data corrections and errata transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The report notes when earlier versions reflected different counts and that edits were made to accurately reflect removals (e.g., corrections to spam/scam and harassment/abusive content counts for Jan–Jun 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows a commitment to correcting and annotating historical data when errors are discovered; corrections are explicitly called out inline with the relevant metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting cadence, units, and presentation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: This report provides details about removals during the six-month period between January 1 and June 30, 2025, and presents historical six-month periods (Jan–Jun, Jul–Dec). Uses notation 'M = millions' and 'K = thousands' for numeric display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the temporal granularity (six-month windows) and numeric unit conventions used throughout the report, enabling consistent interpretation of counts and trends across periods.
